segments.de:
Disclosure of product information for financial products that are marketed on the basis of environmental or social characteristics on the website

relating to the open-ended domestic special AIF with fixed investment terms, in the form of a special sub-fund with a primary investment focus on property and the designation

“ICF GLoG”

a. Summary

This financial product (the “Fund”) promotes environmental/social characteristics but does not have a sustainable investment objective. The investments underlying this financial product do not take into account the EU criteria for environmentally sustainable economic activities within the meaning of the Taxonomy Regulation. This financial product does not take into account the most significant adverse impacts on sustainability factors.

The financial product aims to build a diversified portfolio of logistics properties. At least 75 per cent of the properties’ lettable area must hold DGNB or BREEAM certification.

The financial product plans to invest exclusively in properties and, where applicable, property companies whose scope of business is generally limited to the holding and management of properties and which have no employees.

b. No sustainable investment objective

This financial product promotes environmental or social characteristics but does not aim to make sustainable investments.

c. Environmental characteristics of the financial product

The fund promotes investment in logistics properties, the majority of which hold DGNB or BREEAM certification. Both certification schemes take into account both environmental and social characteristics. DGNB stands for ‘German Sustainable Building Council’. DGNB e. V. is a non-profit and non-governmental organisation dedicated to developing and promoting approaches and solutions for the sustainable planning, construction and use of buildings.

BREEAM stands for ‘Building Research Establishment Environmental Assessment Methodology’ and is a UK-based assessment system for the environmental and socio-cultural aspects of building sustainability. BREEAM was developed by the Building Research Establishment (BRE).

d. Investment strategy

Taking into account its General and Specific Investment Conditions as well as its investment strategy, the financial product aims to maintain a diversified portfolio of logistics properties. At least 75 per cent of the lettable area of the properties must hold DGNB or BREEAM certification. The financial product plans to invest exclusively in property and, where applicable, property companies whose scope of business is strictly limited to the holding and management of property and which have no employees. The financial product will not invest in commercial enterprises; consequently, a corresponding assessment of good governance practices is not required.

e. Allocation of investments

In accordance with its investment strategy, the financial product will invest exclusively in the property asset class. Within this asset class, the focus is on the logistics segment. At least 75 per cent, based on the lettable area of the properties, must hold DGNB or BREEAM certification for the construction of the property or for existing properties. A maximum of 25 per cent, based on the lettable area of the properties, may not hold any certification.

f. Monitoring of environmental characteristics

The respective ratings/awards for the property certifications mentioned under d) (investment strategy) serve as sustainability indicators. The underlying data is monitored on an ongoing basis. Compliance with the required standards for maintaining the respective certifications is also monitored on an ongoing basis.

g. Methods

The Fund’s sustainability criteria are met if at least 75 per cent of the investments in property, based on lettable area, are made in properties that hold a DGNB rating of at least ‘Gold’ or at least a BREEAM ‘Good’ rating for the ‘construction of the property’ or ‘Existing Building’.

h. Data sources and processing

The property-specific data required to obtain the certification referred to under d) (Investment Strategy) is usually provided by sellers during the acquisition process via a digital data room. The data contained therein is generally reviewed and validated as part of technical, legal, tax and economic due diligence. The individual due diligence processes are carried out by specialists such as engineers, solicitors, tax advisers and auditors. During the management phase, the property-specific data is provided and processed by the relevant utility company, Asset Manager or Property Manager, as well as by technical advisers where applicable. Estimates will therefore largely be dispensed with.

i. Restrictions regarding methods and data

The financial product does not impose any restrictions regarding methods and data.

j. Duty of care

All of the fund’s investments are reviewed during the pre-acquisition due diligence phase (and on an ongoing basis during management) to ensure compliance with the requirements for obtaining and/or maintaining the certifications referred to in d). The results of these reviews will be used to assess the investments and, where necessary, any required divestments.

k. Engagement policy

The financial product plans to invest exclusively in property and, where applicable, property companies that do not conduct their own operational business. The financial product will not invest in commercial enterprises, which is why the issue of engagement policy is not relevant to this financial product.

l. Specific benchmark

No overarching benchmark has been defined.

This product information was initially published on 1 July 2023.

Change history:

12 August 2024: Addition of the fund’s ISIN number and the initial publication date.

segments.en:
Disclosure of product information for financial products that promote environmental or social characteristics on the website

regarding the open-ended domestic special AIF with fixed investment conditions in the form of a special investment fund with an investment focus on real estate and the name

“ICF GLoG“

a. Summary

This financial product (the „Fund“) promotes environmental/social characteristics but does not have a sustainable investment objective. The investments underlying this financial product do not take into account the EU criteria for environmentally sustainable economic activities within the meaning of the Taxonomy Regulation. This financial product does not take into account the main adverse impacts on sustainability factors.

The financial product aims for a diversified portfolio of logistics properties. At least 75% of the rental space of the properties must have DGNB or BREEAM certification.

The financial product only plans investments in properties and possibly property companies whose scope of business is fundamentally limited to holding and managing properties and which have no employees.

b. No sustainable investment objective

This financial product promotes ecological or social characteristics, but does not aim for sustainable investments.

c. Environmental or social characteristics of the financial product

The fund advertises that it invests in logistics properties, most of which have DGNB or BREEAM certification. Both certifications take into account both ecological and social characteristics. DGNB stands for „German Sustainable Building Council“. The DGNB e. V. is a non-profit and non-governmental organisation that has set itself the task of developing and promoting ways and solutions for the sustainable planning, construction and use of buildings.

BREEAM stands for „Building Research Establishment Environmental Assessment Methodology“ and is a UK-based assessment system for environmental and socio-cultural aspects of building sustainability. BREEAM was developed by the Building Research Establishment (BRE).

d. Investment strategy

The financial product aims to achieve a diversified portfolio of logistics properties, taking into account its General and Special Terms of Investment and its investment strategy. At least 75% of the rental space of the properties must have DGNB or BREEAM certification. The financial product only plans investments in properties and possibly property companies whose scope of business is fundamentally limited to holding and managing properties and which have no employees. The financial product will not invest in commercial companies, which is why a corresponding assessment of good governance practices is not required.

e. Allocation of investments

In accordance with its investment strategy, the financial product will invest exclusively in the property asset class. Within the asset class, the focus is on the logistics segment. At least 75% in terms of the rental space of the properties have DGNB or BREEAM certification for the construction of the property or in the portfolio. A maximum of 25% of the rental space of the properties have no certification.

f. Monitoring of environmental or social characteristics

The respective ratings/awards of the property certifications mentioned under d) (investment strategy) serve as sustainability indicators. The data on which these are based is monitored on an ongoing basis. Compliance with the values required to maintain the respective certifications is also monitored on an ongoing basis.

g. Methods

The fund’s sustainability criteria are met if at least 75% of the investments in properties are made in relation to the rental space in properties that have a DGNB award of at least „Gold“ or at least BREEAM „Good“ for the „construction of the property“ or „existing property“.

h. Data sources and processing

The property-specific data required to obtain the certification mentioned under d) (investment strategy) is usually provided by the seller during the purchase process via a digital data room. The data contained therein is reviewed and checked for plausibility as part of technical, legal, tax and economic due diligence. The individual due diligence processes are carried out by specialists such as engineers, lawyers, tax advisors and auditors. In the management phase, the property-specific data is provided and processed by the respective utility company, asset or property manager and, if necessary, technical consultants. Estimates are therefore largely dispensed with.

i. Limitations with regard to methods and data

The financial product does not impose any limitations in terms of methods and data.

j. Due Diligence

All of the fund’s investments are reviewed during the purchase due diligence phase (and on an ongoing basis during management) with regard to obtaining and/or maintaining the certifications mentioned under d). The results of the reviews are used to evaluate the investments and any necessary divestments.

k. Participation Policy

The financial product only plans investments in properties and possibly property companies that do not have their own business operations. The financial product will not invest in commercial companies, which is why the topic of participation policy is not relevant for this financial product.

l. Specified Benchmark

An overall benchmark has not been defined.

This product information was initially published on 01.07.2023

History of changes:

12.08.2024: Addition of the ISIN number of the fund and the initial publication date.
